trickyParts: The relaunch decision runs inside the same mutateClaim critical section as the retirement and is persisted with the locator clear in one write, but the relaunch itself (resumeWorker -> deliverToWorker) runs after the lock: deliverToWorker takes the same token's section itself and re-validates the claim.

A dead claim holding a pending prompt but no worker-queue entry is enqueued for the drain rather than handed a catch-up: deliverToWorker drops a catch-up behind a queued assignment and nothing else would deliver it.

markWorkerDead evicts and closes a cached client for the dead process before the retirement's stop, so the resync path never awaits worker_stop_timeout_seconds on a half-open stream; the evicted client's own close event finds the cache moved on.
The FakeRuntime fixture must not seed tree()'s tmux root locator: closeTree probes the root and the fake refuses tmux-shaped locators.
Killing a tmux session's only pane tears the private server down; the relaunch's fresh server may reissue the same pane id, so the live rows compare process identity (sameProcess), never the pane id.
deviations: markWorkerDeadLocked was not kept as a persisting wrapper: it would have been a one-call-site four-line function, so the breaker (retirePromptFailedClaim) calls retireDeadWorkerLocatorLocked and persists itself. The plan's one-write rule for the death path is unchanged.
